Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Kestrel is excited to move forward but procurement raised two practical concerns with Exhibit C as currently written (see attached markup):

1) Pilot vs. enterprise minimums — we run a 90-day pilot that will not meet the annualized minimums in Exhibit C. The language currently exposes us to an early true-up that we cannot realistically forecast. Can Redwood add a "pilot carveout" that waives minimums for the first 90 days or alternatively defines a prorated ramp so that the pilot period is excluded from the annual true-up?

2) Corridor tiebreaker — the current floor/ceiling corridor has an ambiguous tiebreaker when usage lands exactly on a boundary (e.g., 10,000 tokens). We submitted a clean redline that proposes a simple tie-to-higher-band rule, but legal is pushing for an operational example table to be explicit.

We attached a redline of Exhibit C and a short schedule showing our anticipated pilot usage. Can your team confirm what you can accept? We're hoping to finalize commercial terms before our Q4 budget freeze.

Thanks,
Eric

That preserves the economics while giving you runway to evaluate.

- Tie-to-higher-band tiebreaker: operationally straightforward; legal asked for an example. Laura and I will add a worked example (table) to the redline to avoid ambiguity.

Mina / Team / Eric —

I reviewed Kestrel's markup and propose the following compromise language (tracked in the attached PDF):

1) Pilot carveout: add section "Pilot Period; Exclusion from True-Up" with these elements:
   - The "Pilot Period" is defined as the first ninety (90) days following the Service Commencement Date and must be set out in the onboarding checklist. Consumption during the Pilot Period will be excluded from calculation of the Annual Minimum for the first contract year only.
   - If Customer elects to continue with a paid deployment following the Pilot Period, Customer will be eligible for a one-time onboarding credit not to exceed the lesser of 10% of first year committed fees or $75,000, provided an Order Form is executed within sixty (60) days after end of Pilot.

2) Corridor tiebreaker: add a short rule and an example table: "In the event usage equals a corridor boundary, usage shall be assigned to the immediately higher band for purposes of fee calculation." Example table included showing boundary scenarios.

Operational note: we cannot accept a full waiver of minimums for the entire first year — that creates adverse revenue recognition exposure — but the limited exclusion for the Pilot Period plus a capped onboarding credit is reasonable.

Please see attached redline_comparison.pdf for exact language and an example calculation for 10k tokens. Eric, can you confirm the onboarding timeline in your SOW so we can finalize the dates?

Thanks,
Laura

Eric — quick operational follow-up from the billing side:

If we accept the Pilot Period exclusion, billing will treat the Pilot as "trial consumption" and not invoice against the Annual Minimum. To keep invoicing clean we need: (a) a one-line addendum in the Order Form that specifies Pilot start/end dates, and (b) a CSM confirmation email when the Pilot closes. That mirrors other customers we've done this with.

Concession: Redwood is willing to extend the onboarding credit proposed by Laura to $100k (capped) if Kestrel executes the Order Form and SOW within 45 days following the Pilot and commits to a minimum annualized floor for year 2. This is a one-time commercial concession we can advertise to your CFO during procurement.

Next steps: if Eric can confirm by EOD tomorrow that Kestrel accepts the Pilot carveout language and the 45-day execution window, we'll prepare an updated Exhibit C and a clean Order Form addendum for signature.
